summary.headline: Signatureglobal Q1 FY27: pre-sales ~Rs 20bn (20% of Rs 100bn FY target) and collections only Rs 6.7bn, well below the ~Rs 11bn run-rate.
summary.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 pre-sales of about Rs 2,000 crore, led by the Tonino Lamborghini branded-residence launch in Sector 71, Gurugram, priced above Rs 22,000/sq ft with GDV above Rs 4,000 crore. Realisation across the portfolio rose to over Rs 17,000/sq ft from about Rs 15,000 for FY26. Collections fell to about Rs 6.7bn, which management attributed to lumpy milestone payments slipping into next quarter. Management kept FY27 guidance intact: Rs 150bn of new launches, Rs 100bn of pre-sales, and revenue recognition above Rs 50bn, while signalling a land-buying push inside and outside NCR.

financial_highlights.change: Management says it is in line with the ~Rs 2,000-2,500 crore quarterly run-rate; best quarter last year was Q1 FY26 at ~Rs 2,600 crore
Below the ~Rs 1,100 crore per quarter management cites as its norm
vs a little above Rs 15,000/sq ft for FY26

financial_highlights.value: Under Rs 3.9bn (stated as 'less than Rs. 3.9 billion')
financial_highlights.change: Expected to rise modestly during the year as land buying increases

financial_highlights.metric: Average realisation on Q1 revenue recognised (completed inventory)
financial_highlights.change: Affordable-heavy completions; P&L not reflective of current pricing

segments.name: Residential – Gurugram (Sector 71, Tonino Lamborghini branded residence)
segments.commentary: Over 12 acres, >2 mn sq ft SBA, GDV above Rs 4,000 crore; ~800 units, ~400 opened in Phase 1, 300+ sold. Management has crossed Rs 1,500 crore of sales from this launch.

segments.name: Residential – Sector 71 and SPR (upcoming H2 launches)
segments.commentary: Next launches are planned in SPR, with a good portion of FY27 launches in Sector 71 and some outside the micro-markets.

guidance_outlook: New launches of Rs 150bn for FY27 reaffirmed; further launches planned in Q3 (around Diwali) and Q4.
Pre-sales target of Rs 100bn for FY27 maintained; Q1 delivered about 20% of this.
Revenue recognition of more than Rs 50bn for FY27 and a good PAT from historical projects, with projects worth over Rs 5,000 crore to complete this year.
Collections expected to rise through the year; management says Q2 should be good.
Land capex of roughly Rs 1,500-1,800 crore for FY27 in new business development, in core NCR and outside NCR.
Expects construction cost escalation of 7-8% over a decade, to be budgeted; no sharp spike seen in Q1.
capex_capacity: Delivered about 19 mn sq ft to date; about 9 mn sq ft remains under development, with average completion in 2-3 quarters.
Launched about 23 mn sq ft since Feb 2024 (De Luxe DXP), with GDV of Rs 334bn; sales to date of about Rs 230-240bn.
Forthcoming portfolio of about 17 mn sq ft, including 5 mn sq ft of commercial development with RMZ (announced March); another 12 mn sq ft to launch in FY27 and FY28.
Two large townships, of 125 acres and 140 acres, have been launched in Gurugram.
Land and business development to target large low-rise formats of 100-150 acres in core and new markets; mid-income focus for new markets.
demand_pricing: Delhi NCR H1 2026 launches were 18,470 units (+10% YoY) per Cushman & Wakefield; Gurugram accounted for 74% of luxury launches; average launch price up 24% YoY in Q2 2026.
Management says demand is outpacing supply in Gurugram, and developers are taking inflation-plus price increases.
Management says the Middle East conflict caused a macro headwind during Q1, but the Tonino Lamborghini launch sold well.
Each SPR unit is expected at roughly Rs 5-5.5 crore ticket size.
Management said the sales-to-collections timing is driven by construction milestones, so collections lag sales.

qa_highlights.question: Which geographies are being considered for expansion outside NCR, and what land capex is planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is evaluating opportunities and will not name locations yet. Land capex is about Rs 1,500-1,800 crore for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 launches be concentrated in one micro-market, and what are the H2 locations?
qa_highlights.answer: Two of the H2 launches are in SPR, and the third is most likely in SPR too. Some launches will be outside SPR, but Sector 71 holds a large share of the FY27 pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: How do branded-residence launches differ, and how fast will they sell?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says differentiation comes from product, brand, unit size and orientation. Sales target is about 50% within 3-6 months of launch, with inventory released at about 10% a year until completion. Financial closure comes at around 40% sold.

qa_highlights.question: Why were collections weak, and can they reach Rs 2,000 crore a quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 collections were an aberration due to lumpy milestone payments slipping to next quarter. The norm is ~Rs 1,100 crore a quarter, and management expects a good Q2. Sales will convert to collections over time.

qa_highlights.question: What are the cost trends from geopolitical issues?
qa_highlights.answer: No inordinate material or labour cost increase so far. Long-run escalation of 7-8% is budgeted over the coming years.

qa_highlights.question: What product and margin profile will external-market projects have?
qa_highlights.answer: Low-rise, larger-format, mid-income projects are planned to build brand presence and delivery track record in new markets, not small 5-10 acre parcels.

risks_watch: Collections were ~Rs 6.7bn against the ~Rs 11bn norm, so cash conversion depends on slipped milestone payments being received in Q2.
Achieving Rs 100bn pre-sales requires about Rs 80bn over the remaining three quarters, relying on Q3 and launches around Diwali.
Net debt will rise as land buying of Rs 15-18bn is done, against Rs 25bn of cash.
Q1 revenue recognised at under Rs 6,000/sq ft on completed inventory, versus current pricing of Rs 17,000/sq ft; margin mix will shift.
Heavy concentration in Sector 71 and SPR for FY27 launches; new-market entry is still unnamed.
Exposure to Middle East conflict, currency moves and monsoon disruption.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the full-year targets and on demand, but defensive on the weak collections quarter, which was explained as timing. Evasive on the location of out-of-NCR projects and on pricing for them.
key_quotes: Given our launch pipeline, we stay confident of achieving about Rs. 100 billion of pre-sales for the current year.
Collections, yes, this quarter was a bit of an aberration.
We launched the project at the highest ever price we have achieved ever, which is a little above Rs. 22,000 a foot, hence taking the GDV value in excess of Rs. 4,000 crores

~9 mn sq ft under development, average completion in 2-3 quarters
Rs 150bn of new launches for FY27 (further launches Q3 around Diwali and Q4)

growth.why: Management reaffirmed FY27 guidance (Rs 150bn launches, Rs 100bn pre-sales, revenue recognition above Rs 50bn) and plans Rs 1,500-1,800 crore land buying, but Q1 pre-sales were only ~20% of target and collections of ~Rs 6.7bn were well below the ~Rs 11bn run-rate, with no explicit revenue growth % given.
